This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
2.

Heard Mr. Niranjan Maharana, learned counsel for the Petitioners and Mr. Arupananda Das,
learned Additional Government Advocate.

3. This Writ Petition has been filed by the Petitioners to quash the order dated 06.12.2023 passed by the Collector and District Magistrate, Jharsuguda (Opposite Party No.3) vide Annexure-5.
4.

The Collector, Jharsuguda in its order dated 06.12.2023 has held that with regard to the RCP Pada, MCL Authorities submitted that the resident of RCP Pada, Jurabaga have constructed houses over vested land of MCL which is very close proximity to mine working of Belpahar OCM.
In order to smooth shifting of the MCL land, monetary benefits of Rs.2,00,000/- in favour of each eligible resident has been sanctioned and the Petitioner is also included for same benefits.

5. Learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that the houses have been constructed over the land in question and the compensation amount has not assessed properly and it should be on a higher side and moreover, the Petitioners have not received the monetary benefits as yet.

Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 provides that any person interested who has not accepted the award, can file Judhistir Chhanchan & vs State Of Odisha & Others ....

1 written application to the Collector requiring that the matter be referred by the Collector for determination of the Authority, inter alia, the amount of compensation and the second proviso to section 64 of the Act indicates that if the Collector fails to make any such reference within the period so specified, the Applicant may apply to the Authority, as the case may be, requesting it to direct the Collector to make the reference within a period of thirty days.
Admittedly, the Petitioners have not availed the remedy available Under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: At this stage, learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that liberty may be granted to the Petitioners to submit the application before the Collector for making reference to the Authority for determination of the amount.
If any such application is made within a period of two weeks from today, the same shall be taken into account and appropriate order be passed in accordance with law.

It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case.
6. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
